failures.title: Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Crankshaft Bearing Failure - All AJD-V6 3.0 variants
items.whatHappens: The tin-aluminium coating on the crankshaft bearings is susceptible to fatigue and flaking under high load or if oil change intervals are extended. This leads to a loss of oil pressure, a distinct knocking sound from the bottom end on cold starts, and eventually catastrophic engine seizure.
items.repairVsReplace: Once bearing knock is present, the damage is usually widespread. A full reconditioned Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 engine replacement with a machined block and new bearings is the only reliable fix; a simple bearing swap rarely holds long-term.

items.title: Oil Pump and Turbo Contamination - All AJD-V6 3.0 variants
items.whatHappens: As the crankshaft bearings degrade, metal swarf circulates through the oil system. This debris frequently blocks the oil pickup strainer, starves the twin turbochargers of lubrication, and causes simultaneous turbo failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If the turbos have failed due to oil starvation, replacing them without addressing the root cause (the bottom end) will result in rapid repeat failure. A full engine replacement is required to guarantee reliability.

failures.goodYearsLine: While the AJD-V6 3.0 is a refined and powerful unit, the underlying bearing design flaw persists across all production years. Strict adherence to 5,000-7,500 mile oil change intervals is the only documented way to mitigate the risk .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the AJD-V6 3.0
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ As a Specific page type with no distinct sub-codes listed in the inventory, this section focuses on accurate identification and avoiding common, costly misidentifications. The AJD-V6 3.0 engine code is stamped on the engine block and is also recorded on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number". Owners frequently confuse the AJD-V6 3.0 with its predecessor, the AJD-V6 2.7, or the later Ingenium 6-cylinder diesel, the AJ20D6. While the 2.7L and 3.0L share a similar architectural lineage (both derived from the PSA/Ford Lion V6 family), the 3.0L features a longer stroke, twin turbochargers, and a different engine management system. They are not interchangeable. Furthermore, the modern AJ20D6 is an entirely different, in-house JLR design that will not physically fit the X250/X260 or X351 chassis without extensive modification.

relatives.description: The - the outgoing 2.7-litre twin-turbo V6 that suffered from oil pump housing failures and crankshaft issues, which the 3.0L attempted to address but ultimately inherited similar bottom-end vulnerabilities.
The - the modern Ingenium 3.0-litre inline-six diesel that replaced the V6 architecture, featuring a completely different block design, modular construction, and improved long-term reliability.

The - the Land Rover TDV6/SDV6 designation for the exact same PSA/Ford Lion V6 architecture, sharing the identical crankshaft bearing failure risks, oil pump contamination issues, and replacement economics.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJD-V6 3.0 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 engine for sale can be a budget-friendly option, but it carries a severe inherent risk. Unless the seller can provide comprehensive service records proving strict, short-interval oil changes and a recent compression/oil pressure test, you are likely inheriting a ticking time bomb of bearing wear. Learn more about used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most owners, a reconditioned Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 is the only sensible choice. A proper recon will proactively address the engine’s known weaknesses by machining the block, fitting upgraded crankshaft bearings, replacing the oil pump, and installing new twin turbochargers, delivering near-new reliability for the future. Explore reconditioned engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for low-mileage, high-spec XJ Portfolio or XF S projects where the engine is being stripped to the bare block. This allows for line-boring the main bearings, balancing the rotating assembly, and ensuring the engine matches the pristine condition of the flagship chassis. View rebuilt engine services.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting your replacement through our vetted network ensures the work is completed by specialists familiar with Jaguar's complex twin-turbo diesel systems, backed by a nationwide warranty. Check supply and fit availability.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Classic Jaguar XF and XJ diesel models typically hold values between £4,000 and £15,000, depending on mileage, specification, and condition . Because a fully reconditioned Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 engine replacement can approach £9,500, it is crucial to evaluate the vehicle's overall body condition and scrap value before committing to a major mechanical investment. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value first.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 engine typically costs between £6,500 and £9,500 for supply only, with fitted prices ranging from £7,410 to £10,670. Used units start around £3,500 but carry a severe risk of inherited crankshaft bearing wear. Full rebuilt units can exceed £11,000 for high-spec XJ Portfolio applications. Labour typically adds 14-18 hours at £65-£85/hr for an independent specialist.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Jaguar AJD-V6 3.0 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most critical failure on the AJD-V6 3.0 is crankshaft bearing fatigue, where the tin-aluminium coating flakes under load or extended oil intervals. This leads to a loss of oil pressure, a distinct bottom-end knock on cold starts, and eventual engine seizure. As bearings degrade, metal swarf circulates through the oil system, frequently destroying the oil pump and twin turbochargers. Once bearing knock is present, a full reconditioned replacement with a machined block is the only reliable fix.

mainEntity.name: Which Jaguar models use the AJD-V6 3.0 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AJD-V6 3.0 twin-turbo diesel was fitted to the Jaguar XF (X250 and X260 generations) and the Jaguar XJ (X351 generation) between 2009 and 2020. It served as the primary diesel powerplant for Jaguar's executive and flagship saloons. Power outputs typically ranged from 240 hp to 275 hp depending on the specific model tune. It replaced the older 2.7-litre V6 diesel and was eventually succeeded by the Ingenium inline-six.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned AJD-V6 3.0 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: For any Jaguar XF or XJ diesel, a reconditioned AJD-V6 3.0 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the high risk of bottom-end failure. Used engines almost always inherit the same crankshaft bearing fatigue or oil pump contamination that caused the original removal. A proper reconditioned build machines the block, fits upgraded bearings, and replaces the oil pump and turbos to guarantee reliability. Reconditioned units also include comprehensive compression and oil pressure testing.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the AJD-V6 3.0 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can confirm your engine code by checking the V5C registration document under the "Engine Number" field or by locating the code stamped on the engine block. The AJD-V6 3.0 is a 3.0-litre V6 twin-turbo diesel, easily distinguished from the older 2.7L V6 or the modern Ingenium inline-six. Fitting an AJD-V6 2.7 wiring loom or ECU to a 3.0L block will result in incorrect fueling and poor drivability. Both the 2.7L and 3.0L share the Lion V6 architecture, but they are not direct plug-and-play swaps due to displacement and turbo differences.
